healthCheckup.title: National Health Checkup Eligibility
healthCheckup.subtitle: Pick a birth year to see whether you are due for Korea's national health checkup and cancer screenings this year, and which tests you get. Check your parents' too.
healthCheckup.disclaimer: For reference only. Actual eligibility and test items can differ with insurance changes, past checkups and questionnaire answers, so confirm with the NHIS eligibility lookup (1577-1000). Ask a doctor about your results.

in.birthHint: Checkup age is 'checkup year − birth year', regardless of birthday.

memberHint.office: Office workers get checked every 2 years, matching the parity of their birth year.
memberHint.field: Production, field or sales workers get checked every year, regardless of birth year.
memberHint.head: Heads of self-employed households get checked every 2 years at any age.
memberHint.member: Household members of self-employed subscribers get checked every 2 years from age 20.
memberHint.dependent: Dependents of employees get checked every 2 years from age 20.
memberHint.aid: Ages 20-64 get the general checkup; 66+ get the medical-aid life-transition checkup every 2 years.

in.yearNote: Reference: {y} applies the {base} rules as-is and may change.
in.smoker: I currently smoke and have 30+ pack-years
in.smokerHint: 30 pack-years = 1 pack a day for 30 years or 2 packs for 15. Used only for lung cancer screening (ages 54-74).
in.liver: Diagnosed with cirrhosis or hepatitis B/C
in.liverHint: Used only for liver cancer screening (high-risk, age 40+, every 6 months).
in.privacy: Smoking and liver answers are not included in the share link.

dl.label: Deadline
dl.rush: Bookings pile up in December. If you need an endoscopy, book now.
dl.period: The checkup window runs from January 1 to December 31.

copay.ten: 10% copay (free for the bottom 50% by premium)

ex.range: Once between ages {lo}-{hi}, if you haven't had it yet

lipid.name: Dyslipidemia (cholesterol, triglycerides)
lipid.d: Men from 24, women from 40, every 4 years

hepC.name: Hepatitis C antibody test
hepC.d: Once at 56; confirmatory test covered if positive

pft.name: Lung function test
pft.d: Ages 56 and 66 (new in 2026, early COPD detection)

plaque.name: Dental plaque test
plaque.d: Added to the dental exam at 40

colon.name: Colorectal
colon.d: Age 50+ · fecal occult blood test, colonoscopy if positive

liver.name: Liver
liver.d: High-risk age 40+ · liver ultrasound + blood test (AFP)

lung.name: Lung
lung.d: High-risk smokers aged 54-74 · low-dose chest CT

ca.lungHint: At ages 54-74, current smokers with 30+ pack-years can also get lung cancer screening (low-dose CT). Smoking history is taken from a general checkup questionnaire in the past 2 years.
ca.liverHint: With cirrhosis or hepatitis B/C, liver cancer screening (every 6 months) also applies.
ca.fieldNote: Reference: for non-office workers we assume 2-year cancer screenings (stomach, breast, cervical, lung) still follow birth-year parity. Confirm with the NHIS lookup.

plan.title: Schedule and if you miss it
plan.fine: Employers must have employees take the checkup. If they don't, the employer can be fined KRW 100,000-300,000 per worker depending on repeat violations (Occupational Safety and Health Act). Watch for your company's notice.
plan.phone: Eligibility lookup and requests are on the NHIS website or app (login required) or at 1577-1000.

ms.desc: Tap a birth year to see that result. Try your parents' ages too.
ms.note: All ages in the table are even, so these birth years are due for the general checkup that year. Age = checkup year − birth year.

rows.items: Mental health (depression, early psychosis) every 2 years begins; cervical cancer screening begins (women)
Hepatitis B, lifestyle assessment, dental plaque; dyslipidemia begins (women); stomach and breast (women) cancer screening begins
Colorectal cancer screening begins (yearly); lifestyle assessment
Bone density (women); lung cancer screening age begins (high-risk smokers)
Hepatitis C antibody test; lung function test
Lung function, bone density (women), senior physical function; cognitive test begins (every 2 years)

prep.title: Before the checkup
items: Fast from 9 p.m. the night before. Glucose and liver numbers come out accurate, and you can have a gastroscopy.
Bring ID. If you lost the notice, print a confirmation from 'Checkup eligibility' on the NHIS website.
Tell the clinic about daily medication such as blood-pressure, diabetes or anticoagulant drugs when you book.
For the colorectal (stool) test, pick up a sample kit in advance or ask the clinic how to submit it.
Book the cervical test outside your period.

missed.title: If you missed the window
items: National checkups can only be taken from January 1 to December 31 of your eligible year.
The following year you can be added via the NHIS 'previous-year non-attendee' request (1577-1000).
If you were flagged for high blood pressure, diabetes and the like, the confirmatory test is available until March 31 of the next year.
December gets crowded, so book in October or November.

company.title: Company checkup vs. national checkup
items: For employees, the national general checkup also counts as the statutory workers' general health exam. The checkup your company arranges is usually this one.
Office workers take it every 2 years, non-office workers every year. If the employer doesn't arrange it, it can be fined KRW 100,000-300,000 per worker.
If your company pays for a comprehensive checkup, ask the clinic whether the national items are included and billed to NHIS.
Dependents (family members) book a clinic themselves, independent of the company.

tips.title: Booking tips
items: Use NHIS 'Find a checkup clinic' to search nearby clinics by checkup type.
Taking the general checkup and cancer screenings at one clinic on the same day gets it all done at once.
The bottom 50% by premium and medical-aid recipients pay nothing for cancer screening. Colorectal and cervical screening are free for everyone.
Results arrive by mail or under 'Checkup results' on the NHIS website.

items.q: Who is due for the 2026 health checkup?
items.a: 2026 is an even year, so people born in even years such as 1976 or 1986 are due for the general checkup. Household members and dependents must be 20 or older (born 2006 or earlier), and non-office employees are due every year regardless of birth year. Confirm on the NHIS website or app.

items.q: Is checkup age the international (birthday-based) age?
items.a: No. It is 'checkup year − birth year', regardless of birthday. For example, 56 in 2026 means born in 1970, and the age-56 items (hepatitis C antibody, lung function) are given within that year.

items.q: At what age does national cancer screening start?
items.a: Stomach: 40+ every 2 years (gastroscopy). Colorectal: 50+ yearly (fecal occult blood test). Breast: women 40+ every 2 years. Cervical: women 20+ every 2 years. Liver: high-risk 40+ every 6 months. Lung: current smokers aged 54-74 with 30+ pack-years every 2 years.

items.q: How much does the checkup cost?
items.a: The general checkup is free (fully paid by NHIS). Cancer screening has a 10% copay, but colorectal and cervical are free, and the bottom 50% by premium and medical-aid recipients get all cancer screenings free.

items.q: What if I can't go by December 31?
items.a: That year's window closes, but the following year you can be added through the NHIS 'previous-year non-attendee' request. Employers are obliged to have employees checked and can be fined if they don't.

items.q: Is the company checkup different from the national checkup?
items.a: For employees, the general checkup is both the national checkup and the statutory workers' general health exam. Office workers take it every 2 years, non-office workers every year. Ask the clinic whether a company-paid comprehensive checkup includes the national items.

From 2026, people aged 56 and 66 get a lung function test (early COPD detection). Since 2025, a hepatitis C antibody test at 56, mental health screening every 2 years at 20-34 (depression and early psychosis), and a bone density test for women at 60 were added.

items.q: Can I get a colonoscopy through the national checkup?
items.a: Currently people 50+ take a yearly fecal occult blood test and get a colonoscopy if it is positive (free). The government aims to introduce colonoscopy every 10 years for ages 45-74 by 2028, but it is not final yet.
